text:
Kirill Marchenko scored three times for Toronto, one of them on a chance the model rated below 1%, and it still wasn't enough. Buffalo came back from two goals down and won 5-4 in overtime, a result that matched the way the game was played over its full length. BUF ended with 3.29 expected goals to TOR's 2.87 and 61 shot attempts to 47, which gave the Sabres a 57% deserved-to-win share.

Toronto led for most of the first two periods. Marchenko's power-play goal at 13:10 of the first, a between-the-legs finish, put the Leafs up 2-1, and his second and third goals in the middle period stretched it to 4-2. Jack Quinn answered both times Buffalo needed it, tying the game in the first and again in the second. Toronto even held the edge in expected goals through the first two periods (1.19 to 0.81 in the first, 1.50 to 1.22 in the second).

The third period flipped it. BUF out-chanced TOR 0.88 to 0.12 in expected goals, and Dennis Gilbert (10:05) and Mattias Samuelsson (12:16) scored 2:11 apart to level it at 4-4. Owen Power won it at 3:14 of overtime on a feed from Quinn, who finished with two goals and two assists. Sergei Bobrovsky allowed 1.7 more goals than his shots deserved, and TOR managed just 0.18 expected goals across the third and overtime combined.
